institutionName: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To enjoy my Erasmus stay, culture, food, weather. A break from everyday life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. University of Copenhagen does a great job assisting and providing information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not as much information about practical things, courses etc. as I am used to from my home university. It seems like the approach in Greece is more laissez faire. However, there was never a reason to stress about anything as eventually everything worked out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Many opportunities to find housing on social media platforms. I found accommodation on a Facebook group.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I found that HousingAnywhere and Facebook had the best options. It may be a good idea to become a part of the WhatsApp Erasmus chats, as you can exchange experiences about landlords and ask people if they have a spare room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There really was no formal registration process. Every course is 'open' and you can show up and take the exam if you like. For me, it was important that I passed at least 30 ECTS for my home university, which was not a problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Most of the professors were really helpful in asking questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful since I could freely select the classes I wanted. I ended up changing my Learning Agreement once, because I wanted some courses that were taught on the same days.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about it. I believe you have 4 weeks to change your Learning Agreement from the first day of class, and if you have any questions, the professors are helpful in answering questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty of the subjects varied greatly. Most were somewhat easier than I am used to. The exams are not that demanding, but it is necessary to study to pass. All in all, I think it's balanced considering it's Erasmus courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching also varied greatly. Some professors used powerpoints, others didn't. Some professors included the students a lot, while others didn't. I'm more used to interaction between the students and the professors at my home university, which was not used that much at the host university, where it was primarily the professor who talked for 1-2 hours.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Labor Law, Maritime Law, Intellectual Property Law, Introduction to Greek Civil Law and International Telecommunications Law. 5 courses in total

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely Labor Law, Intellectual Property Law and Maritime Law. I believe these are the most interesting. However, Intellectual Property Law was more demanding than the other courses, but I thought it was worth it for the academic benefits.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries in the supermarket are not as cheap as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a university gym, but it was located about an hour from the Law School, hence no students were really using it. A lot of activities are arranged by Erasmus Student Network (ESN), which can definitely be recommended to look out for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the islands, go on hikes around Athens. Go to the beach of course. Also, go to Istanbul if you haven't been - flights are very cheap from Athens.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Same as above. Also, just go out and enjoy the good food and culture. Athens is very big and every neighborhood is different

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. All courses are completely full of Erasmus students, so most of the time you'll be around people from all kinds of places.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yes, definitely check out the ESN instagram page (ESN Kapa Athens) and attend some activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Public transport is not the best compared to Copenhagen, where I'm from. Can be quite frustrating if you're in a hurry.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Greeks are very social, and there is not a lot of stress around you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy yourself and have fun. Don't go to Athens if you're focusing on improving academically, but only if you want a calm semester where you can experience a lot. Don't cook at home too often - go out and eat instead. It's very cheap and there's a lot of good restaurants to pick from.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: What I did was picking courses so I only had to attend school three days a week, which was great since I had long weekends every week and therefore also the freedom to go on trips etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people and having the freedom to do fun stuff

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't think I faced any great challenges on my exchange other than the frustration of public transport - especially busses that never arrive on time and are always packed with people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
